page: Amazon Web Services m5a.16xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 7571 processors running at 2.5 GHz, delivering 64 virtual CPUs across 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is paired with 256 GB of DDR4 system memory clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard general-purpose ratio of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include AVX, AES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration flags, though it lacks newer vector extensions such as AVX-512 or AMX.

Network connectivity features a 12 Gbps baseline throughput without bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The instance does not include any local instance storage, requiring users to attach networked storage such as Amazon EBS for persistent filesystem operations. Similarly, the platform features no GPU accelerators, keeping its footprint concentrated on general x86 compute and memory capacity.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear profile favoring aggregate parallel throughput over single-core execution speed. Single-core tests show constrained performance, with Geekbench single-core scoring 726.0 and stress-ng single-core in the lower decile. Conversely, multi-core metrics scale cleanly, reflected in an average Geekbench multi-core score of 7646.0, an overall PassMark CPU score of 37125.27, and strong cryptographic throughput on PassMark CPU encryption at 51802.43. Memory bandwidth delivers 122.43 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 59.86 GB/sec for writes.

This hardware profile delivers cost efficiency when consolidating multi-threaded enterprise services that do not depend on high per-core clock rates. The instance sustains 36.14 million Redis SET operations per second and handles 19.6 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. It is well matched for mid-tier distributed relational databases, Redis caching layers, background batch processing, Clang compilation pipelines, and containerized web application clusters.
description: Amazon Web Services m5a.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The configuration provides 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores and 256 GB of DDR4 memory, establishing a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory balance. It features a 12 Gbps baseline network interface, no bundled local storage, and zero integrated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations indicate modest single-thread execution speeds alongside stable multi-core parallel performance and strong cryptographic processing. Memory subsystems yield up to 122.43 GB/sec on uncached read operations. The instance is suited for multi-threaded services that distribute load across numerous threads rather than demanding ultra-fast single-core clock speeds, making it an effective choice for distributed databases, caching clusters, software build pipelines, and general enterprise application hosting.
